label: Descriptive versus reference-fixed naming of GOD_4 under the necessary-being box
summary: Owner-queued slice (step 2 of 5, refs #1784): Kripke-style naming senses at the God-existence stage, connecting the idle rigid-designation library (MODAL-RIGID-DESIGNATION) to the root route. Analyst formulations, attribution deferred; Naming and Necessity was not read or cited (its source-search attempt stays blocked). Findings. (1) The stage-one naming premises (reduced e39a4fce, fuller 1ec205ed, MaximeEnsIsGod 957a71fe) are non-modal: they evaluate the name in one model, and at the reference world the descriptive (GOD_NAMING_1) and reference-fixed (GOD_NAMING_2) senses designate the same bearers (Laws clause 2), so these premises are neutral between the readings; no sense choice is hidden in them. (2) The readings diverge only under a box, and there only for a description that varies by world. The box K node (cdf897a8) applies the world-independent GOD_4 predicate to one fixed root and boxes its existence. It is logically equivalent to its GOD_NAMING_2 reading (rigidIffBoxK in the controls result, through TruthCore.Results.Modal.RigidDesignation.laws), and equally to its GOD_NAMING_1 reading with the route's own world-independent description GodAt := fun _ => sigma.IsGod (DescConstIffBoxK), since both bridges then hold trivially. So the route's 'God exists necessarily' is the actual God's existence at every accessible world under either sense with that description; the route's 1ec205ed is used only at the selected world. (3) For a world-varying GodAt (deliberately not identified with sigma.IsGod) the GOD_NAMING_1 reading (necessarily, something existing uniquely meets the description) is a different proposition: neither it nor the box node entails the other in general (two-world separations: in explicit models where the corresponding bridge fails, that direction fails). It gives the box node with the open bridge NoOtherPossibleGod (only the actual GOD_4 could meet the description at an accessible world); the box node gives it with GodhoodEssentialToGod and NoOtherPossibleGod; a joint model satisfies all four. (4) Necessity of identity (question 2): for reference-fixed names with one actual bearer, co-designation persists to every accessible world where the bearer exists, and strict necessary co-designation is equivalent to necessary existence; for descriptive names actual co-designation need not persist even when the bearer exists (control). The route's identities (first mover = maximum, De ente source = GOD_4 root) are de re equalities of Lean terms, so they need no Kripke principle; the principle concerns names and never supplies the necessary existence the box node asserts, which comes from the route's own 25 inputs. (5) Rival assessment under the substantive-objection standard: the route models GOD_4 and the classical attributes as world-independent predicates applied at w. That is an implicit modelling commitment that divinity and the attributes are essential to the root n, not an absence of claims about other worlds. GodAt is introduced to test it, and the two open bridges (together: at accessible worlds an existing y meets GodAt exactly when it is GOD_4) are its explicit form for the descriptive reading. With that qualification, the Kripke point that a reference-fixing description need not hold of its bearer at other worlds yields no substantive objection to any existing route step: no step derives anything from attributes at other worlds, and the commitment is now visible as the two bridges. The descriptive node is close to the deDictoK sense of NecessarySenseFork and strictly stronger than its box clause (it requires a unique existing satisfier). The descriptive reading's two bridges are open; positive support in the classical framework is the identity of God with his deity and the incommunicability of the divine nature (ST I q.3 a.3, q.11 a.3; supports, not attributed or formalized here). The separating models are formal interpretations only, not evidence against either bridge. Rejected readings: a third Lean sense for 'a name whose sense is the description' (it has the world-intension of GOD_NAMING_1 under narrow scope and of GOD_NAMING_2 under wide scope; the remaining difference, what is knowable a priori, is not modal-semantic); registering rigid-to-box as a strength order (the two are equivalent; recorded with logically_equivalent_to); registering a one-way argument from the GOD_NAMING_2 node to the box K node (built and verified, then withdrawn: it lowered the expanded-route diagnostic of the root route from 16 to 13 only by replacing four premises with one leaf equivalent to the conclusion, which is a restatement, not support).
blocker: GodAt is a primitive world-indexed predicate; the route's description vocabulary (InAct, MoreIn, CausesIn, ComponentOf) is world-invariant, so the bridges NoOtherPossibleGod and GodhoodEssentialToGod cannot yet be derived from the route's own premises. Next test: index the nominal description (NominalGod) by worlds over a shared frame and try to derive GodhoodEssentialToGod from an esse-is-essence premise and NoOtherPossibleGod from at-most-one subsistent being across accessible worlds.
